claims: The term "Antichrist" appears in 1 John and 2 John.
The term "Antichrist" does not appear in Revelation.
The term "Antichrist" refers to anyone denying Jesus is the Christ or Messiah.
The term "Antichrist" describes a person who pretends to be the Christ.
The Bible refers to "many antichrists" already present.
The Antichrist concept combines the "man of sin" from 2 Thess 2:3-4.
The Antichrist concept combines the "beast" from Rev 13.
St. Paul described the Antichrist as setting himself up in God’s temple claiming to be God.
The Antichrist has historically been associated with figures like Nero.
Reformers like Luther and Calvin associated the Antichrist with the Pope.
In Islamic eschatology, a similar figure is Al-Masih ad-Dajjal.
The "Man of Lawlessness" is from 2 Thess 2.
The "Man of Lawlessness" is a specific singular figure who will appear before the Second Coming.
The "Beast from the Sea" is from Rev 13.
The "Beast from the Sea" represents a political/military power that persecutes Christians.
Roman emperors like Nero or Julian the Apostate were considered foreshadowing agents of the Antichrist.
Catholic Answers Podcasts describe the primary function of the Antichrist as mirroring or parodying Jesus Christ to deceive
